H_hierarchical.evidence: The paper mentions stance and swing being divided into sub-modes, but the controller is presented as a flat four-mode finite-state gait model with no explicit composite-state semantics.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Transitions use multiple measurable guards: heel strike via socket load cell, ankle dorsiflexion angle threshold, foot-off via ankle torque load cell, and knee velocity becoming negative.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: Each mode selects continuous knee and ankle impedance behavior; torque is computed from stiffness, damping, equilibrium angle, joint angle, and velocity with per-mode parameters.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: No controller fault state, emergency stop, rollback, or from-any-state recovery transition is described; safety harnesses are experimental equipment, not STM recovery logic.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: Mode names and transition prose are in Section 3.2/Fig. 9, while the executable impedance equation and per-mode parameter tables are separated into Eq. (3) and Tables 4/5.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Gait terms such as heel strike, push-off, foot-off, and maximum flexion require biomechanics interpretation into sensor events or thresholds.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: The main mode actions are stated in the same Section 3.2 paragraph as the mode definitions; later tables refine parameters rather than introducing unrelated prose-only actions.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: The transition guards are single-event or single-threshold conditions; no guard combines multiple variables with arithmetic or boolean composition.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: No parent/composite state has its own entry, during, or exit behavior beyond child modes.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: The paper does not declare any fault-triggered transition that applies from all modes to a safe state.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: There is no deep composite state or non-trivial initial pseudo-state chain.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: Guards are simple gait-event thresholds, not arithmetic-plus-boolean expressions suitable for SMT consistency checking.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: The same continuous impedance torque law applies across all four gait modes with mode-specific parameters, so an aspect/during action could avoid duplicating per-state torque logic.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: Some mode effects are described functionally, such as impact absorption and push-off, but the controller is still mainly specified as concrete knee/ankle torque and impedance behavior.

one_line_pitch: A flat but action-heavy powered-prosthesis gait supervisor where sensor guards select continuous knee and ankle impedance laws, stressing action extraction more than hierarchy or recovery.
rationale: The paper gives a real four-mode finite-state gait controller with meaningful sensor guards and strong state-dependent continuous torque actions. It is a good stress test for action extraction and moderate guard extraction, especially because the impedance law and per-mode parameters are distributed across text, equation, figures, and tables. It is secondary rather than top-tier because hierarchy is only a gait-phase grouping and there is no explicit fault or global recovery model.
